---
title: "R bytecode compiler written in C"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 3
    df_print: kable
params:
  ## The --csv reports of crbcc_bench.py. install has the suite install, from
  ## the image build. compile has the suites check and compile, from the CI.
  install: "install.csv"
  compile: "compile.csv"
  ## If this value is not empty, the report writes two files for the crbcc
  ## README to this directory: the figure install-time-top15.png and the
  ## shields.io badge speedup.json.
  assets: ""
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, dev = "png", dpi = 120)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(reactable)

## The categorical slots 1-2 of the dataviz reference palette, in a fixed order.
COL   <- c(gnur = "#2a78d6", crbcc = "#eb6834")
INK   <- "#0b0b0b"  # primary text
INK2  <- "#52514e"  # secondary text, axes
GRID  <- "#e4e3df"  # grid lines
RANGE <- "#c3c2b7"  # line between the compilers in a dot plot
COMPILERS <- names(COL)

## This list is the same as in crbcc_bench.py.
RECOMMENDED <- c("MASS", "lattice", "Matrix", "nlme", "survival", "boot",
                 "class", "cluster", "codetools", "foreign", "KernSmooth",
                 "mgcv", "nnet", "rpart", "spatial")

fmt   <- function(x, digits = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
pct   <- function(x) paste0(fmt(100 * x, 0), "%")
times <- function(x, digits = 1) paste0(fmt(x, digits), "x")
gmean <- function(x) { x <- x[is.finite(x) & x > 0]; exp(mean(log(x))) }
pkg_group <- function(package) if_else(package %in% RECOMMENDED, "recommended", "CRAN")
## GNU R time / crbcc time. NA if it is not defined, for example for 0 / 0.
ratio <- function(gnur, crbcc) { r <- gnur / crbcc; r[!is.finite(r)] <- NA; r }
## A Markdown link to a crbcc commit on GitHub, with the short hash as text.
commit_link <- function(commit) {
  if (!grepl("^[0-9a-f]{40}$", commit)) return(sprintf("`%s`", commit))
  sprintf("[`%s`](https://github.com/PRL-PRG/crbcc/commit/%s)", substr(commit, 1, 7), commit)
}

## The colDefs of the columns <m>_gnur, <m>_crbcc, <m>_diff and <m>_ratio.
## The column group gives the unit.
compare_cols <- function(m, digits, ratio_digits = 2) {
  num <- colFormat(digits = digits, separators = TRUE)
  setNames(list(colDef(name = "GNU R", format = num), colDef(name = "crbcc", format = num),
                colDef(name = "diff", format = num),
                colDef(name = "ratio", format = colFormat(digits = ratio_digits, suffix = "x"))),
           paste0(m, c("_gnur", "_crbcc", "_diff", "_ratio")))
}
## A table that the reader can search and sort. The columns must be numeric,
## because the sort uses the values, not the formatted text.
sortable <- function(data, columns, groups)
  reactable(data, columns = c(list(package = colDef(minWidth = 95, sticky = "left"),
                                   group = colDef(minWidth = 95)), columns),
            columnGroups = groups, searchable = TRUE, pagination = FALSE, height = 600,
            compact = TRUE, highlight = TRUE, style = list(fontSize = "13px"),
            defaultColDef = colDef(minWidth = 51, headerStyle = list(whiteSpace = "nowrap")))

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(
  text = element_text(colour = INK2),
  axis.text = element_text(colour = INK2),
  axis.text.y = element_text(colour = INK),
  legend.text = element_text(colour = INK),
  strip.text = element_text(colour = INK, hjust = 0, size = 11),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = INK2),
  legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left", legend.title = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = GRID, linewidth = 0.3),
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)))
compiler_fill   <- scale_fill_manual(values = COL, breaks = COMPILERS)
compiler_colour <- scale_colour_manual(values = COL, breaks = COMPILERS)
## Without drop0trailing, the labels of a duplicated axis can have a
## different number of decimals than the labels of the main axis.
log_x <- function(...) scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma(drop0trailing = TRUE), ...)
log_y <- function(...) scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_comma(drop0trailing = TRUE), ...)

# Read the CSV files -------------------------------------------------------

## Returns the "# key: value" header (meta) and the rows (data) of a CSV file.
read_bench <- function(file) {
  lines <- readLines(file)
  meta <- sub("^# ", "", grep("^#", lines, value = TRUE))
  data <- read.csv(text = grep("^#", lines, value = TRUE, invert = TRUE),
                   colClasses = "character")
  list(file = basename(file),
       meta = as.list(setNames(sub("^[^:]*: ", "", meta), sub(": .*", "", meta))),
       data = mutate(data, run = as.integer(run), value = as.numeric(value)))
}
ins <- read_bench(params$install)
clo <- read_bench(params$compile)

## A run with a failure still has its rows. The statistics do not use them.
RUN <- c("suite", "benchmark", "compiler", "run")
failed_runs <- function(d) d |> filter(failure != "") |> distinct(across(all_of(RUN)), failure)
passed <- function(d) anti_join(d, failed_runs(d), by = RUN)
failed_table <- function(d) {
  f <- failed_runs(d)
  if (nrow(f) > 0)
    knitr::kable(mutate(f, failure = gsub("\\s+", " ", failure)),
                 caption = "Failed runs. The statistics do not use these runs.")
}

## The environment of a benchmark, from the header of its CSV file.
env_list <- function(b) {
  m <- b$meta
  cat(sprintf("- Machine: `%s`, %s %s, %s logical CPUs%s\n", m$hostname, m$system,
              m$machine, m$logical_cpus, if (is.null(m$cpu_model)) "" else paste(",", m$cpu_model)),
      sprintf("- Start: %s UTC\n", sub("T", " ", substr(m$timestamp, 1, 16))),
      sprintf("- %s\n", m$r_version),
      sprintf("- crbcc %s, commit %s\n", m$crbcc_version, commit_link(m$crbcc_commit)),
      sprintf("- Raw data: [%s](%s)\n", b$file, b$file), sep = "")
}

# Install benchmark --------------------------------------------------------

## One row for each package, with the median of the runs for each metric and
## compiler, for example elapsed_gnur. Only the packages with results of the
## two compilers. The longest elapsed_gnur is first.
ins_runs <- n_distinct(ins$data$run)
pk <- passed(ins$data) |>
  filter(suite == "install") |>
  group_by(package = benchmark, compiler, metric) |>
  summarise(value = median(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(metric, compiler), values_from = value) |>
  filter(!is.na(elapsed_gnur), !is.na(elapsed_crbcc)) |>
  mutate(group = pkg_group(package), .after = package) |>
  arrange(desc(elapsed_gnur))

## The totals of all packages and of each group. less is the part of the
## GNU R elapsed time that crbcc saves.
tot <- bind_rows(pk, mutate(pk, group = "all")) |>
  group_by(group = factor(group, c("all", "CRAN", "recommended"))) |>
  summarise(packages = n(), across(matches("_(gnur|crbcc)$"), sum)) |>
  mutate(rest_gnur = elapsed_gnur - native_gnur - bytecode_gnur,
         rest_crbcc = elapsed_crbcc - native_crbcc - bytecode_crbcc,
         less = 1 - elapsed_crbcc / elapsed_gnur)
less <- setNames(tot$less, tot$group)
bc_share <- setNames(tot$bytecode_gnur / tot$elapsed_gnur, tot$group)
n_grp <- setNames(tot$packages, tot$group)
el <- c(gnur = sum(pk$elapsed_gnur), crbcc = sum(pk$elapsed_crbcc))

# Compile benchmark data ---------------------------------------------------

chk <- filter(clo$data, suite == "check")
n_chk <- sum(chk$value[chk$metric == "closures"])
chk_failed <- failed_runs(chk)
## The failure of a check gives the count: "<n> closures differ or do not
## compile".
n_bad <- sum(as.integer(regmatches(chk_failed$failure,
  regexpr("[0-9]+(?= closures differ)", chk_failed$failure, perl = TRUE))))
cl_runs <- n_distinct(clo$data$run[clo$data$suite == "compile"])
n_cl_pkg <- n_distinct(clo$data$benchmark[clo$data$suite == "compile"])

## One row for each closure: the median compile time of each compiler, the
## size in AST nodes, and the size class (powers of 10). Only the closures
## with results of the two compilers.
cl <- passed(clo$data) |>
  filter(suite == "compile", metric == "compile") |>
  group_by(package = benchmark, closure, size = as.numeric(size), compiler) |>
  summarise(time = median(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = compiler, values_from = time)
n_missing <- sum(is.na(cl$gnur) | is.na(cl$crbcc))
cl <- cl |>
  filter(!is.na(gnur), !is.na(crbcc)) |>
  mutate(class = cut(size, c(1, 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4, Inf),
                     c("1-9", "10-99", "100-999", "1,000-9,999", ">= 10,000"), right = FALSE))

## One row for each package: the median run time of each compiler. The time
## of a run is the sum of the compile times of its closures. Only the
## packages with results of the two compilers.
cl_pk <- passed(clo$data) |>
  filter(suite == "compile", metric == "compile") |>
  group_by(package = benchmark, compiler, run) |>
  summarise(time = sum(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(package, compiler) |>
  summarise(time = median(time), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = compiler, values_from = time) |>
  filter(!is.na(gnur), !is.na(crbcc))
cmp <- c(gnur = sum(cl_pk$gnur), crbcc = sum(cl_pk$crbcc))
cmp_ratio <- cmp[["gnur"]] / cmp[["crbcc"]]
## The headline: the geometric mean of the closure speedups. It does not use
## a closure with a zero time, because its speedup is 0 or infinite.
speedup <- gmean(cl$gnur / cl$crbcc)
n_zero <- sum(cl$gnur == 0 | cl$crbcc == 0)
largest <- slice_max(cl, size, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
largest_name <- paste0("`", largest$closure, "`")

n_chk_pkg <- n_distinct(chk$benchmark)
if (nrow(chk_failed) == 0) {
  correct_tldr <- sprintf("crbcc gives the same byte code as GNU R for all %s closures of %d packages.",
                          fmt(n_chk, 0), n_chk_pkg)
  correct <- sprintf("The check compiled %s closures of %d packages. All closures have the same byte code with the two compilers.",
                     fmt(n_chk, 0), n_chk_pkg)
} else {
  failed_counts <- sprintf("failed for %d of %d packages and %s of %s closures",
                           nrow(chk_failed), n_chk_pkg, fmt(n_bad, 0), fmt(n_chk, 0))
  correct_tldr <- paste0("the check ", failed_counts, ".")
  correct <- paste0("The check ", failed_counts, ":")
}

# Badge for the README -----------------------------------------------------

if (nzchar(params$assets)) {
  dir.create(params$assets, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  writeLines(sprintf('{"schemaVersion": 1, "label": "compile speedup", "message": "%s faster than GNU R", "color": "blue"}',
                     times(speedup)),
             file.path(params$assets, "speedup.json"))
}
```

# Introduction

crbcc compiles R code to byte code. It gives the same byte code as the GNU R
`compiler` package, but it is faster.

- [README and source code](https://github.com/PRL-PRG/crbcc#readme)
- [Use crbcc](https://prl-prg.github.io/crbcc/crbcc.html): compile closures
  and install packages with crbcc
- [crbcc on CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=crbcc)

# Benchmarks

The two benchmarks ran on different machines, at different times, and
possibly with different crbcc versions. Do not compare the times of one
benchmark with the times of the other.

## TL;DR

- **Install time** ([install benchmark](#install-benchmark), crbcc
  `r ins$meta$crbcc_version`): with crbcc, `R CMD INSTALL` of `r nrow(pk)`
  packages takes `r pct(less[["all"]])` less time than with GNU R
  (`r fmt(el[["crbcc"]])` s, not `r fmt(el[["gnur"]])` s).
- **Compile time** ([compile benchmark](#compile-benchmark), commit
  `r commit_link(clo$meta$crbcc_commit)`): crbcc compiles closures
  `r times(speedup)` faster than GNU R. This value is the geometric mean of
  the speedups of `r fmt(nrow(cl), 0)` closures of `r n_cl_pkg` packages.
- **Correctness** ([compile benchmark](#compile-results)):
  `r correct_tldr`

## Install benchmark {#install-benchmark}

### Methodology {#install-methodology}

The benchmark installs `r n_distinct(ins$data$benchmark)` packages: the
`r sum(!unique(ins$data$benchmark) %in% RECOMMENDED)` CRAN packages with the
most downloads and the `r sum(unique(ins$data$benchmark) %in% RECOMMENDED)`
recommended packages. Each install is `R CMD INSTALL` of the CRAN source
tarball. It runs `configure` and compiles the native code with
`MAKEFLAGS=-j8`. For each package, `r ins_runs` runs with GNU R come first,
then `r ins_runs` runs with crbcc. The installs run one at a time.
The benchmark sets `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` for each R process, because one
OpenBLAS thread for each CPU adds CPU time that depends on the machine.

Each install goes into an empty library. Thus all dependencies come from the
image library, which GNU R compiled.

For crbcc, R reads the hook `inst/r-cmd-install-hook.R`, which replaces the
byte-code compiler with crbcc. In each R process,
`inst/benchmarks/timing-profile.R` measures the time in two functions. It
only reads the clock. Each run gives three numbers:

- **elapsed**: the wall time of `R CMD INSTALL`.
- **native**: the time in `tools:::.shlib_internal`, which compiles and links
  the C, C++ and Fortran code.
- **bytecode**: the time in `compiler:::tryCmpfun`, which compiles each
  closure to byte code.

The value of a package is the median of its runs. A total is the sum of the
package values. The rest is elapsed - native - bytecode. In this time, R
parses the code, makes the lazy-load database and the help pages, and loads
the package to test it. The statistics do not use failed runs.

The tables compare the two compilers:

- **diff**: the GNU R time minus the crbcc time. If it is positive, crbcc is
  faster.
- **ratio**: the GNU R time divided by the crbcc time. If it is above 1,
  crbcc is faster. If it is not defined, for example for a package without
  native code, the cell is empty.
- **share**: the GNU R time of a metric divided by the GNU R elapsed time.

The image build ran this benchmark with the crbcc of the image. Thus the
results are for that crbcc, not for the commit of the compile benchmark.

```{r install-env, results = "asis"}
env_list(ins)
```

### Results {#install-results}

```{r install-failed}
failed_table(filter(ins$data, suite == "install"))
```

With crbcc, the elapsed time is `r pct(less[["all"]])` less for all
`r n_grp[["all"]]` packages: `r pct(less[["CRAN"]])` less for the
`r n_grp[["CRAN"]]` CRAN packages and `r pct(less[["recommended"]])` less for
the `r n_grp[["recommended"]]` recommended packages. With GNU R, the
byte-code compile time is `r pct(bc_share[["all"]])` of the elapsed time.

```{r install-totals}
tot |>
  pivot_longer(matches("_(gnur|crbcc)$"), names_to = c("metric", ".value"), names_sep = "_") |>
  group_by(group) |>
  mutate(share = gnur / gnur[metric == "elapsed"]) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(group, factor(metric, c("elapsed", "native", "bytecode", "rest"))) |>
  transmute(packages = if_else(metric == "elapsed", sprintf("%s (%d)", group, packages), ""),
            metric, `GNU R (s)` = fmt(gnur), `crbcc (s)` = fmt(crbcc), `diff (s)` = fmt(gnur - crbcc),
            ratio = times(gnur / crbcc, 2), share = pct(share))
```

The package with the longest GNU R elapsed time is first. The right panel
gives the byte-code share of each package.

```{r install-time-plot, fig.height = 1.5 + 0.25 * nrow(pk)}
## A dot plot of the packages in p, in the order of p, and a bar plot of the
## byte-code share. The share has a linear axis, thus it is a separate plot
## next to the dot plot. If top is TRUE, the X axes are also at the top,
## because the plot of all packages is tall.
install_plot <- function(p, top = TRUE) {
  p <- mutate(p, package = factor(package, rev(package)))
  time <- p |>
    select(package, matches("^(elapsed|bytecode)_")) |>
    pivot_longer(-package, names_to = c("metric", "compiler"), names_sep = "_") |>
    mutate(metric = factor(metric, c("elapsed", "bytecode"),
                           c("elapsed time of R CMD INSTALL (s)", "byte-code compile time (s)"))) |>
    ggplot(aes(value, package)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = package), colour = RANGE, linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = compiler), shape = 21, colour = "white", size = 3.2, stroke = 0.8) +
    compiler_fill + log_x(sec.axis = if (top) dup_axis() else waiver()) +
    labs(x = "s (log scale)", y = NULL) +
    facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x")
  share <- p |>
    mutate(metric = "GNU R byte-code share of elapsed") |>
    ggplot(aes(bytecode_gnur / elapsed_gnur, package)) +
    geom_col(fill = COL[["gnur"]], width = 0.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)),
                       sec.axis = if (top) dup_axis() else waiver()) +
    labs(x = "% (linear scale)", y = NULL) +
    facet_wrap(~ metric) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())
  ## The two plots have the same rows, thus the packages align.
  cbind(ggplotGrob(time), ggplotGrob(share), size = "first")
}
## The README shows the first 15 packages.
if (nzchar(params$assets))
  ggsave(file.path(params$assets, "install-time-top15.png"), install_plot(head(pk, 15), top = FALSE),
         width = 9, height = 1.5 + 0.25 * 15, dpi = 120, bg = "white")
grid::grid.draw(install_plot(pk))
```

The table gives the package values in the order of the plot. To sort the
table, click a column header.

```{r install-table}
ins_tab <- select(pk, package, group)
for (m in c("elapsed", "native", "bytecode")) {
  gnur <- pk[[paste0(m, "_gnur")]]
  crbcc <- pk[[paste0(m, "_crbcc")]]
  ins_tab[paste0(m, c("_gnur", "_crbcc", "_diff", "_ratio"))] <- list(gnur, crbcc, gnur - crbcc, ratio(gnur, crbcc))
}
ins_tab$bytecode_share <- pk$bytecode_gnur / pk$elapsed_gnur
el_cols <- compare_cols("elapsed", 2)
na_cols <- compare_cols("native", 2)
bc_cols <- compare_cols("bytecode", 3)
sortable(ins_tab,
  columns = c(el_cols, na_cols, bc_cols,
              list(bytecode_share = colDef(name = "share", format = colFormat(percent = TRUE, digits = 0)))),
  groups = list(colGroup("elapsed (s)", names(el_cols)), colGroup("native (s)", names(na_cols)),
                colGroup("bytecode (s)", c(names(bc_cols), "bytecode_share"))))
```

## Compile benchmark {#compile-benchmark}

### Methodology {#compile-methodology}

The closures of a package are its namespace functions, its S4 methods and its
R6 methods (`crbcc:::package_closures`). The check uses `r n_chk_pkg`
packages: the base packages without `datasets` and `tcltk`, and the packages
of the install benchmark. The timed runs use only the `r n_cl_pkg` packages of
the install benchmark. The counts are closures, not compile events. Thus they
do not compare with older reports.

First, the check compiles each closure one time with each compiler, and
compares the byte code (`crbcc:::identical_strict`). A closure fails the
check if the byte code differs or a compiler stops with an error. Then each
compiler compiles each closure in `r cl_runs` runs, and the benchmark
measures the time of each `cmpfun()` call. Before these calls, each run
compiles its first closure one time without a measurement, because the first
compile loads code of the compiler. As in `R CMD INSTALL`, the R JIT is off.
A run is one R process for one package and one compiler. The benchmark sets
`OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1` for each R process, because one OpenBLAS thread for
each CPU adds CPU time that depends on the machine. For each package, the
GNU R runs come first, then the crbcc runs. Each run compiles the closures in a
different random order.

The time of a run is the sum of the compile times of its closures. The value
of a package is the median of its run times. A total is the sum of the package
values. The value of a closure is the median of its runs. A total includes the
garbage collections and the lazy loads of a run. The closure values do not
include them, because the random order moves them to a different closure in
each run.

The speedup of a closure is its GNU R time divided by its crbcc time. The
compile speedup in the TL;DR and in the README badge is the geometric mean of
the speedups of all timed closures. In this mean, each closure has the same
weight. In the ratio of the totals, which the results also give, the large
closures have more weight. If a closure has a zero time, its speedup is not
defined, and the geometric means do not use it. If a closure has times of
only one compiler, the statistics do not use it. In this report,
`r n_zero` closures have a zero time and `r n_missing` closures have times of
only one compiler.

For a group of closures, for example a package, the speedup is the geometric
mean of the closure speedups. The size of a closure is the number of AST nodes in its body and in the default
values of its formals (`crbcc:::function_size`). The statistics do not use
failed runs. In the table of the packages, diff and ratio compare the
totals, as in the install benchmark.

The benchmark ran in the benchmark image, with the crbcc of the commit below.

```{r compile-env, results = "asis"}
env_list(clo)
```

### Results {#compile-results}

`r correct`

```{r check-failed, eval = nrow(chk_failed) > 0}
chk_failed |>
  transmute(package = benchmark, failure = gsub("\\s+", " ", failure))
```

```{r compile-failed}
failed_table(filter(clo$data, suite == "compile"))
```

The timed runs compiled `r fmt(nrow(cl), 0)` closures of `r n_cl_pkg`
packages. The compile speedup, the geometric mean of the closure speedups, is
`r times(speedup)`. GNU R compiles the closures in `r fmt(cmp[["gnur"]], 2)` s,
and crbcc in `r fmt(cmp[["crbcc"]], 2)` s. Thus the ratio of the totals is
`r times(cmp_ratio)`.

The median closure size is `r fmt(median(cl$size), 0)` AST nodes. The
largest closure is `r largest_name` in `r largest$package`, with
`r fmt(largest$size, 0)` nodes.

```{r size-table}
cl |>
  group_by(`size (AST nodes)` = class) |>
  summarise(closures = fmt(n(), 0),
            `gnur median (us)` = fmt(median(gnur) * 1e6),
            `crbcc median (us)` = fmt(median(crbcc) * 1e6),
            `gnur / crbcc geo. mean` = times(gmean(gnur / crbcc)))
```

```{r size-time-plot, fig.height = 6}
long <- cl |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(COMPILERS), names_to = "compiler", values_to = "time") |>
  mutate(compiler = factor(compiler, COMPILERS))
mid <- long |>
  group_by(compiler, class) |>
  summarise(size = median(size), time = median(time), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(long, aes(size, time * 1e6, colour = compiler)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.9, alpha = 0.3, stroke = 0) +
  geom_line(data = mid, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = mid, aes(fill = compiler), shape = 21, colour = "white",
             size = 3, stroke = 0.8) +
  compiler_colour + compiler_fill + log_x() + log_y() +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1))) +
  labs(x = "closure size (AST nodes, log scale)", y = "compile time (us, log scale)",
       subtitle = "The points are closures. The line is the median of the size class.")
```

```{r size-speedup-plot, fig.height = 4.5}
x <- cl |> mutate(speedup = gnur / crbcc) |> filter(is.finite(speedup), speedup > 0)
mid <- x |>
  group_by(class) |>
  summarise(size = median(size), speedup = gmean(speedup), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(x, aes(size, speedup)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.9, alpha = 0.35, stroke = 0, colour = COL[["crbcc"]]) +
  geom_line(data = mid, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = mid, colour = INK, size = 2.5) +
  log_x() + log_y() +
  labs(x = "closure size (AST nodes, log scale)", y = "speedup, gnur / crbcc (log scale)",
       subtitle = "The points are closures. The line is the geometric mean of the size class.")
```

The table gives the totals and the closure speedup of each package. The
sizes are in AST nodes. The package with the longest GNU R total is first.

```{r compile-package}
cmp_tab <- cl |>
  group_by(package) |>
  summarise(closures = n(), size_median = median(size), size_max = max(size),
            speedup = gmean(gnur / crbcc)) |>
  inner_join(cl_pk, by = "package") |>
  arrange(desc(gnur)) |>
  transmute(package, group = pkg_group(package), closures, size_median, size_max,
            total_gnur = 1e3 * gnur, total_crbcc = 1e3 * crbcc, total_diff = total_gnur - total_crbcc,
            total_ratio = ratio(gnur, crbcc), speedup)
tot_cols <- compare_cols("total", 1, ratio_digits = 1)
count <- colFormat(digits = 0, separators = TRUE)
sortable(cmp_tab,
  columns = c(list(closures = colDef(name = "count", format = count),
                   size_median = colDef(name = "median size", format = count, minWidth = 85),
                   size_max = colDef(name = "largest", format = count)),
              tot_cols,
              list(speedup = colDef(name = "geo. mean", format = colFormat(digits = 1, suffix = "x"),
                                    minWidth = 105))),
  groups = list(colGroup("closures", c("closures", "size_median", "size_max")),
                colGroup("total compile time (ms)", names(tot_cols)),
                colGroup("closure speedup", "speedup")))
```
